clue.text: Tom’s family are revolting? Yes

blocks.note: the family of Tom Thumb, the tiny folk-tale hero, would be the Thumbs
people in revolt are up in arms, or risen up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Tom's whole family are in open rebellion, and the answer comes back yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, but here it means rising in rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised thumb gesture signals approval or agreement, standing in for an affirmative reply.

clue.text: President sounds like sincere guy

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is heard as these words when spoken

blocks.note: a sincere fellow is a true man

explanation.surface: A head of state is described as coming across as an honest fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry S. Truman was the thirty-third President of the United States, serving 1945 to 1953.

clue.text: Where half of grub finishes up?

definitions.text: Where half of grub finishes up?

indicators.note: half of a word keeps just one of its two halves, here the back end

blocks.note: the second half of grub
finishes are ends

explanation.surface: A riddle asks where the last of someone's dinner ends up after being washed away.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: food scraps washed down a sink lodge in the curved trap of the drainpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved section of waste pipe under a sink traps water and catches debris such as washed-away food.

clue.text: Something waiter offers might be found in old barrel

indicators.note: the answer is said to be findable within these letters once they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant server's offering is supposedly lurking inside an ancient cask.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant staff commonly bring a small baked loaf or basket of bread to diners before the meal.

clue.text: Nub?

blocks.note: surface reading: the gist or small knob of something
setter's reading: the word for a small sweet roll written back to front, a baked treat turned over

explanation.walkthrough: Nub is bun spelt backwards, so it is a bun inverted, which is the name of a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert is baked with fruit at the bottom of the tin, then turned over to serve.

clue.text: Moves quickly around but finally stops boat moving

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps itself about another
finally points to the closing letter of the word next to it

blocks.note: to moor a vessel is to tie it up so it stops drifting
the last letter of but

explanation.surface: A pilot speeds about the harbour yet in the end must halt the drifting vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: MOORS goes around T to give MOTORS.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is informal for travelling fast, as a car or runner speeding along.

clue.text: Rock star’s partner, very loud and unreliable

blocks.note: Yoko Ono was John Lennon's wife
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A famous musician's partner is described as loud and not to be relied on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on-off is intermittent, working one moment and failing the next, so it cannot be depended upon.

clue.text: Reforming constitution of our islet reveals anomalies

indicators.note: reforming the make-up of something means rebuilding it in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rewriting the governing charter of a tiny island exposes some irregularities.
explanation.definitionFit: Outliers are data points or cases lying far from the rest, things that do not fit the pattern.

clue.text: Relatives died after being taken in by aerobics commercials

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held within it

blocks.note: step is a form of aerobics, and ads are commercials
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Family members pass away after being drawn in by fitness advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepfather is a parent by marriage, so stepdads are family members related through a remarriage.

clue.text: Betrayed anxiety seeing step taken by unionists with part of NI

blocks.note: a pace is a single step
the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party
and means together with
County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Political nerves show as unionists march through a corner of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking back and forth restlessly is the classic outward sign of a nervous, worried person.

clue.text: To reduce consumption is futile

blocks.note: consumption is use
to reduce consumption is to use less

explanation.surface: A cynic declares that any attempt to cut back on consumption is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'to reduce consumption' is read as the two words USE LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless achieves nothing, exactly like a futile effort that brings no result.

clue.text: One taken in by amateurish demo tape, wasting millions

indicators.note: something amateurish is badly put together, so the letters are jumbled
wasting means losing or throwing away, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A band's rough demo recording loses its big money on the way to someone being fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from DEMO TAPE, then rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A child taken in by a new family through legal adoption is an adoptee.

clue.text: Attached and confused when left out

indicators.note: left out means omitted, and left also gives the letter to drop

blocks.note: addled means muddled or confused
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone feels both fastened on and bewildered when excluded from the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added has been appended or joined on, as an attached note is added to a letter.

clue.text: Sickly dip feeder’s unhealthily prepared

indicators.note: something sickly is out of sorts, so the letters are in poor order

blocks.note: taken as written, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: Whatever this ailing snack-dipper eats is made in an unwholesome way.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked by immersion in hot fat is widely regarded as bad for health.

clue.text: Happy dog given ball rolled over, getting indulged

indicators.note: given here means having something put inside it
rolling over turns something end to end so it reads the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
a ball is round, like the letter O
to humour someone is to indulge their wishes

explanation.surface: A contented dog with a ball rolls on its back and is spoilt with attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' means having the ball put inside, before the whole thing is turned round; 'rolled over' could also suggest the dog's trick, which is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone good-humoured is cheerful and pleasant in temper, a fuller way of saying happy.

clue.text: Philosophical work just squeezing in movement of tribe

indicators.note: squeezing something in means forcing it inside another piece
movement of letters means they shift into a new order

blocks.note: just means merely, only
taken as written

explanation.surface: A treatise is described as barely managing to include a people's migration.
explanation.walkthrough: On Liberty is John Stuart Mill's essay; 'movement' looks like a political cause but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill's 1859 essay on individual freedom is a classic text of political philosophy.

clue.text: One with contract taking pair of idiots in

blocks.note: an ass is a fool, so two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A businessman under contract takes on two fools.
explanation.walkthrough: A contract in underworld slang is an agreement to kill someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer works under a contract, the gangland term for a paid commission to murder.

clue.text: Laxative’s working? Don’t get cross: it’s drivel

indicators.note: a cross is the letter X, and not getting it means leaving it out
working means in action, so the letters are set moving into new places

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the medicine has kicked in and is told to stay calm, as it is all nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Drivel here is the verb meaning to dribble saliva, not the noun meaning nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To drivel in its older sense is to let spit run from the mouth, which is what drooling glands do.

clue.text: Readily accept stories: ‘Caught butterflies’

indicators.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so these words are taken by ear

blocks.note: to swallow a story is to believe it without question
stories are tales

explanation.surface: A gullible collector believes the tale that some butterflies were netted.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallow tales, said out loud, is the butterfly's name; the quotation marks disguise 'Caught' as part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowtails are a family of large butterflies with tail-like projections on their hindwings.

clue.text: Become more enthusiastic about motion, oddly, following open hostility

indicators.note: oddly says to keep the letters in the odd-numbered positions

blocks.note: war is open conflict
the first, third and fifth letters of motion

explanation.surface: A debater comes round to a proposal after an initially fierce reception.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm to a person or idea is to grow fonder of it, the phrasal verb for increasing liking.

clue.text: With sharp points, tip removed, still with sharp points

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, and it is taken off

blocks.note: a thorned stem bristles with prickles

explanation.surface: A spiky object loses its point yet stays spiky.
explanation.walkthrough: THORNED loses its first letter; both words describe pointed things, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal with horns carries pointed bony growths on its head, so it bears pointed projections.

clue.text: Dictator’s goal, essentially: police force is something essential in life

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda
the two central letters of goal
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A tyrant's real aim is a police force he regards as vital to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins, compounds every living organism needs.

clue.text: Orpington vacantly hosting carnival centre presenting seven notable stars

indicators.note: vacantly means emptied, so only the outside letters remain
a host holds something within, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Orpington
Rio de Janeiro is famed as the home of carnival

explanation.surface: A Kent town stages a festival at its heart with seven celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: Orpington is a suburban town in south-east London, formerly in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter constellation is identified by seven bright stars, including Betelgeuse, Rigel and the three of its belt.

clue.text: I like this codeword

blocks.note: first meaning: a cry of approval from an audience
second meaning: the word for B in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The radio alphabet uses Alpha, Bravo, Charlie for A, B, C.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is shouted to applaud a fine performance and also serves as the spoken code for one letter.

clue.text: Surrounded by the blue and green?

definitions.text: Surrounded by the blue and green?

blocks.clueFragment: Surrounded by the blue and green?
blocks.note: surface reading: a place encircled by sky and grass, like a countryside scene

blocks.clueFragment: Surrounded by the blue and green?
blocks.note: setter's reading: out on the ocean and turning green in the face

explanation.walkthrough: The blue is a common name for the sea, and green describes a queasy complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller nauseated by a ship's motion is out on open water and pale-faced with queasiness.

clue.text: Ransome represented people in boats

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Arthur Ransome, author of Swallows and Amazons, wrote about children sailing dinghies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers who propel a vessel with oars are by definition people sitting in boats.

clue.text: Mustn’t take heart of intended then mess about

indicators.note: the heart of a word is everything inside it, so the outer letters go
to mess about with something is to scramble it out of order

blocks.note: intended without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A warning not to steal a fiancé's affections and then toy with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the answer means there is no obligation, a looser sense than a prohibition; the setter treats the two negative modals as interchangeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are negative modal verbs telling someone an action should not happen, so one can stand in loosely.

clue.text: Silly money Europe spent on Microsoft software: honestly!

indicators.note: silly means foolish and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
something spent is used up and gone, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Europe
Word is Microsoft's word-processing program

explanation.surface: Someone is aghast at how much European cash was wasted on Microsoft programs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' reads as money being paid out, but it says the E for Europe is used up and gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of surprise or a pledge of truthfulness, like saying honestly.
